criteria.quote: "Ivysaur smells sweet. Why is its back counting down?"
criteria.revision: Replace with: "A sweet smell comes from Ivysaur’s back—but Pokédex entries say it is evidence of a large flower about to bloom." This makes the unusual claim concrete while preserving the question of how the signs connect.

criteria.quote: "Sunlight makes the bud on its back grow larger." / "When large, the bulb seems to stop Ivysaur standing upright." / "sweet aroma means a large flower blooms soon."
"Ivysaur smells sweet, but why is its back counting down?"
criteria.revision: Change the open loop to: "Ivysaur’s sweet smell is a bloom signal—but why do its sunlight, swelling bud, and heavy back all point toward the same moment?" This keeps the tension tied to the specific documented clues rather than the unsupported metaphor of a literal countdown.

criteria.quote: "Now the swelling bud sends a sweet aroma outward."
criteria.revision: Make Scene 4 a sharper evidentiary step: "Another entry adds the missing link: when the bud starts swelling, a sweet aroma wafts from it." This distinguishes swelling-plus-aroma from the opening mystery and makes the progression toward the bloom reveal clearer.

criteria.quote: "The twist: sweet aroma means a large flower blooms soon."
criteria.revision: Do not reveal the twist in the title or premise. Change the title from "Why Ivysaur’s Sweet Smell Is a Bloom Countdown" to "Ivysaur’s Sweet-Smell Signal," then hold the explicit claim that the smell is evidence of a large flower blooming soon until Scene 5.

criteria.quote: "Ivysaur smells sweet." / "Now the swelling bud sends a sweet aroma outward." / "sweet aroma means a large flower blooms soon."
criteria.revision: Give each scent mention a distinct job: make Scene 1 only the mystery ("A sweet aroma comes from Ivysaur’s back"), Scene 4 the swelling-bud evidence, and Scene 5 the meaning of that evidence. Avoid calling the scent a bloom countdown before the final reveal.

criteria.quote: "The scent is not a random trait: after the bud grows larger and heavier, it signals a large flower will bloom soon."
criteria.revision: Replace with: "Sunlight can make Ivysaur’s bud grow larger, and a large bulb can affect how it stands. But the sweet smell is the clearest clue: it is evidence that the large flower will bloom soon." This resolves the chain without claiming that every listed sign is one proven causal sequence.

criteria.quote: "Sweet scent or sunlight: which bloom clue would you trust?"
criteria.revision: Replace with: "Which clue would you trust more: the sweet smell, explicitly described as evidence of bloom, or Ivysaur spending more time lying in sunlight, another sign its bud will bloom soon?" This gives viewers two documented signs with meaningfully different kinds of evidence.
